title: license file
description: A license file of elderlygate/mankit/license/v2 on disk, as nw-licenser writes it and mankit's licenses package reads it: a Resource (ADR-S15) whose spec holds the payload's bytes exactly as signed and the Ed25519 signature over them, so an app checks the file offline against the keys its build trusts (ADR-L1, L5, L6). The signature covers the payload alone. One license file per user, in the org's config folder, read by every app; a trial's file, with its started record, in its app's own folder (ADR-L8); the mankit README gives both paths. Several app versions read it at once: apiVersion, kind and metadata never change; spec may grow (ADR-S15). A file that is not this shape is refused as unreadable.

apiVersion.description: The form the file is in, so a reader knows which schema it meets (ADR-S15, apiversion/v1/forms.yaml). elderlygate/mankit/license/v1 is mankit/v1's license-file.

spec.description: The signed license: the payload's bytes and the signature over them, and for a trial the unsigned record of the trial it started. Open: a newer nw-licenser or app may add fields here, and an older app accepts them (CT-RULE-4).

payload.description: The signed bytes, standard base64: JSON that meets license-payload.schema.json. Kept as bytes, not as an object, so the signature is checked over exactly what was signed.

started.description: The trial this file started, written by the app beside the signed payload (ADR-L9). The signing tool writes the file without it; the app adds it when it writes its built-in trial as its trial file on a start with no license, and writes it anew when the app is reinstalled or updated. Unsigned, as the trial is signed once per product line but starts once per install: the signature covers the payload alone, so this record never breaks it. Editing or deleting it, or touching the binary, gives a fresh trial, as a reinstall does; this is accepted (ADR-L1, L9), and it never opens more than the signed payload names. A rule no schema can say, as the kind sits inside the signed payload: only a trial's file has it. Open: a newer app may add fields here, and an older app accepts them (CT-RULE-4).

day.description: The day the trial started, an RFC 3339 date in UTC, never after the payload's until when it has one. The trial runs the payload's days from it, so license-show.schema.json's licenses[].trialEnds for this file is reckoned from it.
